nodes.evidence: ASan crash-stack frame #1 is ParseTracePacket at proto_trace_parser.cc:306:5, the container dispatch `if (packet.has_power_rails()) ParsePowerRails(packet.power_rails());`. The power_rails submessage was admitted and control entered ParsePowerRails on the observed crashing path (parser-admitted / R1).

`protos::pbzero::PowerRails::Decoder evt(blob.data, blob.size);` is the first parse of the untrusted PowerRails submessage. It executes on the crashing path: it is straight-line-before the sink at 863 inside the same function, and the crash at 863 proves the function ran past 852 (has_rail_descriptor() branch taken).

`auto idx = desc.index();` materializes the attacker-controlled uint32 rail index. Deterministic protobuf-varint decode of the PoC RailDescriptor bytes `08 ff ff ff ff ff 20` (field 1, index varint) yields the full varint 0x107FFFFFFFF, truncated to uint32 idx = 0xFFFFFFFF (4294967295). This is the value that flows to the size guard (858), the resize argument idx+1 (859), and the OOB subscript (863). Runtime execution of 857 is witnessed by asan_reproduce (straight-line predecessor of the 863 sink, same function, same iteration).

The only guard on idx is `if (power_rails_strs_id_.size() <= idx)`; there is NO upper bound on idx. The fix (fbd7bc47) inserts `if (PERFETTO_UNLIKELY(idx > 256)) continue;` immediately after `uint32_t idx = desc.index();` (fix source line 848) and before this size guard. Patch differential on the identical PoC (same sha256): vul image SEGVs at 863, fix image exits 0. vul-crash AND fix-clean together prove the missing upper bound at this site is the root cause.

`power_rails_strs_id_.resize(idx + 1);` executes because size (0) <= idx. idx + 1 is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic; for idx = 0xFFFFFFFF (decoded above) idx + 1 wraps to 0, so resize(0) does not grow the vector. The crash mechanism REQUIRES that resize(idx+1) fail to make idx a valid index: had idx+1 grown the vector to cover idx, the 863 store would be in bounds and there would be no crash. The observed OOB store at 863 (asan_reproduce) is consistent only with the wrapped/ineffective resize; the wrap magnitude is decode-derived (poc_decode), the resize execution and its OOB consequence are runtime-witnessed.

ASan crash-stack frame #0: SEGV at proto_trace_parser.cc:863:33 (column 33 = the `=` store) in ParsePowerRails. `power_rails_strs_id_[idx] = InternString(counter_name)` subscripts the (too-small) vector at idx and stores to a wild address 0x0000ffff7fff. DEDUP_TOKEN and full crash stack reproduce byte-for-byte with sanitizer_trace.txt. StringId = uint32_t (confirmed in trace_storage.h:49), so power_rails_strs_id_ is a std::vector<uint32_t> subscripted OOB. ASan decodes the raw wild-addr SEGV as a READ; OSS-Fuzz classifies it as UNKNOWN WRITE (the operation is a vector-element store).

edges.evidence: Adjacent ASan frames #1 (306) -> #0 (ParsePowerRails); the dispatch fired and the callee entered on the crashing path.

The untrusted PowerRails blob parsed at 852 exposes the rail_descriptor iterator whose current entry is decoded into desc, and desc.index() supplies idx at 857. Straight-line data flow inside the executed function body.
idx (materialized at 857) is the operand of the size guard at 858; the guard is evaluated on the crashing iteration.
The empty vector (size 0) satisfies size <= idx, so the resize branch executes; without it the subsequent subscript could not have run to the observed fault.

edges.via: idx used as the subscript power_rails_strs_id_[idx]
edges.evidence: The store faults at a data-dependent wild address determined by idx (the untrusted uint32 rail index), witnessing that desc.index() flowed unchanged into the OOB subscript on the crashing iteration.

edges.via: wrapped/ineffective resize leaves the vector too small for idx before the store
edges.evidence: resize(idx+1) runs before the 863 store; because idx+1 wrapped to 0 for idx=0xFFFFFFFF (poc_decode) the vector stays empty, so the ordered store at 863 is out of bounds and SEGVs (asan_reproduce).

root_cause_criterion.evidence: The vulnerable code has no upper bound on the attacker-controlled uint32 idx between its materialization (857) and its use as a resize size (859) / subscript (863). The fix adds exactly `if (PERFETTO_UNLIKELY(idx > 256)) continue;` right after idx is read, skipping oversized indices. Same-PoC differential: vul crashes at 863, fix (with the cap) exits 0 -> root_cause_confirmed. A valid alternative framing is the missing cap on the resize argument idx+1 (whose 32-bit wrap is the integer-overflow half of the bug); both frame the same absent upper-bound guard on idx.

deferred.reason: A single-file instrumented rebuild was attempted in the n132/arvo:14018-vul container (installed ninja 1.7.1, extracted the exact cxx/link commands, patched proto_trace_parser.cc with an fprintf of idx and vector size). Compilation fails because the ARVO image stripped the bundled third-party protobuf HEADERS (buildtools/protobuf/src/google/protobuf/*.h absent), so proto_trace_parser.cc cannot be recompiled at all in this image, and a full rebuild also fails (third-party .cc sources absent). Not a budget limit — the sources/headers are simply not present. Function entry (asan_reproduce), root-cause region (patch_differential), sink line (asan_reproduce), and the idx value (deterministic protobuf-varint decode of the PoC) are already witnessed. Run a fresh coverage/DFSan build on a native amd64 host with full third-party sources to add exact-line counters and a direct idx print.
